whatItDoes: Watch a fleet of workflows and relaunch whichever member has fallen off its cadence. Reads its own event log to work out what is late, then lets a model choose from a fixed list of safe moves — code does anything irreversible. Observe-only mode reports what it would launch.
longDescription: The Brain coordinates a fleet of agents, watching for the member that silently misses its run. Each cycle is a four-step loop: scan reads its own Postgres event log into plain facts; assess hands those to a model that may only pick from a fixed list of moves, re-checked in code; actuate launches the right member behind guardrails; report writes a Slack briefing and the run back to the log. Observe-only mode reports what it would launch.
notes:
Click **Use this template** — Sapiom builds and deploys it for you, then run it from the workflow page. Your $5 signup credit covers first runs.

Out of the box it orchestrates a two-member demo fleet that both launch `hello-agent`, so it runs end to end with nothing else deployed. To point it at your own fleet, deploy those child workflows first and pass your `fleet` in the run input — a child can't be launched until it has been deployed. For the Slack briefing, supply `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` and pass a `briefingChannelId`; without them it just logs the briefing. Run it with `{ "observeOnly": true }` to have it report what it would launch without launching anything.

Prefer to work from the code? Run it locally with `run_local` and `{ "dryRun": true }` to trace the whole scan → assess → actuate → report loop for free — the real model call still runs, only the network side effects are skipped — or edit and deploy it with the Sapiom MCP.

requiredSecrets.label: Slack bot token
requiredSecrets.description: A Slack bot token (`xoxb-…`) with `chat:write`. Without it the briefing is returned in the run's output and nothing is posted.

settings.label: Slack channel or user id
settings.description: Where the daily briefing is posted. Leave it empty and the briefing stays in the run's output.
